data.name: Ashtar
data.gender_notes: Ashtar is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In pre-Islamic Arabian mythology, Ashtar was a goddess of war and fertility. She was also known as Al-Lat and was revered for her strength and courage. The name Ashtar carries the meaning “Goddess of war” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ashtar usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of war and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ashtar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of war.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashtar total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ashtar" finds its origins in the ancient pre-Islamic Arabian culture. Ashtar was one of the primary goddesses in the Arabian pantheon, known for her goddess of war and fertility. Her association with warfare reflects the martial culture of Arabia, while her connection to fertility reflects the emphasis on agriculture and nature-based beliefs in early Arab society.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic context, the name "Ashtar" loses its pre-Islamic goddess connotation. Instead, it is perceived as a beautiful and evocative name with no particular spiritual significance attached to it. For some, it may hold a personal or emotional significance as a name for a loved one or a spiritual reminder of deep feelings or associations, unrelated to the ancient goddess of the same name. Some may also view it as a nod to the rich cultural heritage of the Arab and Islamic world. Ultimately, it represents the freedom and creativity found in choosing a name that resonates with one's personal and spiritual identity.

historical_references.reference: Ashtar was a pre-Islamic goddess of the ancient Arabian city of Palmyra, identified with Astarte of the Phoenicians, and with Venus by the Greeks. She was the consort of the god Hubal and was considered the goddess of fertility and the protector of the palace and the city walls.

According to some Islamic traditions, Ashtar or Ishtar was a name given to Bilqis, the queen of Sheba. She is mentioned in the Quran as one of the great queens of the past and is described as ruling over a prosperous kingdom with a strong economy and a just rule.
historical_references.time_period: Queen Bilqis, mentioned in the Quran (circa 6th Century AD)
